name: Dominican Republic
headline: Dominican Republic: +2.1% growth in 2025, 3.9% inflation, debt 59% of GDP
sections: Dominican Republic is a $128 billion economy (2025), the world's 68th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.1% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $29K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.3% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 12.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 59% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 72% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.6% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −1.2% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 51% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.9% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 50% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 73.9 years (2024). Population: 10.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
